rules: One question. If a page answers three questions it answers none of them well.
Facts with sources. Every specification links the listing or official page it was read from, on the row it supports.
No invented experience. No “we tested”, no “in our kitchen”, no implied ownership.
No numbers we cannot publish. No price, star rating or review count until Amazon serves or supplies them.
Arithmetic labelled as arithmetic. A ratio we worked out is shown as ours, never as Amazon’s.
A named gap. Each guide ends by stating what it cannot tell you and where to check it yourself.

category_snapshot.heading: In the category right now
category_snapshot.body: Amazon publishes no search-volume or conversion figures to affiliates, so this site does not invent a trend. What it can do is date an observation of a page that does exist. On 2026-11-16, Amazon’s own Best Sellers in Air Fryers list (browse node 17659096011, which states on itself that it is “Updated frequently”) showed the Emeril Lagasse 26QT at position #6 in the category, alongside sibling nodes for Air Fryer Ovens and Deep Fryers. That is a snapshot of a list on a date — not a quality judgement, not a rank we awarded, and not a reason to buy. Prices and star ratings shown on that page are deliberately not repeated here: they may only be displayed when Amazon serves them in a link or supplies them through its API.

duplication_note: Why this set exists alongside The Crisp Report. Two research sessions published guides against the same brief on the same day, from the same three listings. Rather than delete one, the reader set is The Crisp Report — eleven pages, with images and structured data — and this set stays as a second-source check: the same facts quoted independently, with the register id each row rested on. Where the two disagree, the disagreement is a finding, not a style difference, and it belongs on the flagged page.
